kinds.crash: the participant died instead of answering: what came back is a signal, not a message. The corpus counts it with the refusals, because no comparable schema was produced, and that is where it stops being the same thing - an engine that says it does not support a plan and an engine that dies on one are not in the same condition, and only the second is a defect whatever the support

duckdb-dies-while-refusing.what: Two mark joins and eight set operations the extension does not implement. It does not refuse them: the process dies on SIGSEGV, and the corpus sees exit 139 rather than the NotImplementedException the same build raises for the neighbouring cases. Each case runs in a process of its own for exactly this reason, or one of them would take the run with it.

DUCKDB.note: that issue reports the crash as happening while the error is formatted, and names unsupported join and set operations, which is these ten cells

acero-dies-on-an-aggregate-emit.what: An emit mapping over an aggregate whose grouping keys the consumer never read. Acero applies emit elsewhere - it answers five of the seven emit cases and refuses the sixth, the join, with a message naming what it wanted - and here two defects meet: the grouping references are dropped, so the aggregate's output schema has no fields, and the emit index is not range-checked before it indexes that schema, so the process dies on SIGSEGV instead of refusing.

ACERO.note: apache/arrow#50634 reports that the consumer drops AggregateRel-level grouping expressions referenced by expression_references, and apache/arrow#50635 reads them. The exact corpus case passed at PR head 3d2b564f9722a55fe0b74743ffded9378b7a802a with emit [2,0], the expected required bool/int64 schema and all three groups; that change is not merged or present in the pinned PyArrow 25.0.1 measurement. apache/arrow#51243 is the other half: GetEmitInfo indexes input_schema->field(map_id) with no range check, and ProcessEmitProject does the same on the project path, where ProcessExtensionEmit in the same file already returns Status::Invalid. A read with two fields and emit [5] or [-1] dies with no aggregate anywhere, so apache/arrow#50635 stops this case from crashing without making an out-of-range mapping safe
